cards.title: Calibrated Bose-Hubbard chain Hamiltonian
cards.role: Defines every exact-dynamics target and its calibrated couplings.

checks.reason: Main Eq. 1 and supplement Eq. S24 give the same Hamiltonian; Table S1 supplies all J and U values.
Each hopping term is paired with its Hermitian conjugate and diagonal interaction/on-site terms are real.
Quoted MHz frequencies are converted to angular rad/ns by 2*pi*1e-3 before multiplication by time in ns.

cards.title: Fixed-particle occupation-basis matrix elements
cards.role: Turns EQC001 into exact finite matrices without a full tensor-product Hilbert space.

checks.reason: The supplement specifies a local three-level basis and QuTiP bosonic operators for the two-photon simulation.
The enumerated sectors have dimensions 11 for one photon, C(13,2)=78 for two bosons on 12 sites, and C(12,2)=66 in the hard-core sector.
Every hopping event removes and creates one boson, while diagonal terms preserve occupation; total particle number is invariant.

cards.numerical_form: Enumerate occupation tuples with fixed total N and optional per-site cap; add J_j*sqrt(n_j*(n_{j+1}+1)) for j to j+1 and its reverse.

cards.title: Coherent short-time evolution

source_refs.value: Numerical simulation; decoherence neglected because the evolution time is much shorter than T1 and T2

cards.role: Advances every initial Fock state on the paper time grid.

checks.reason: Supplement numerical-simulation text states that decoherence is not included in the theoretical results.
For Hermitian H, exp(-iHt) is unitary and preserves state norm.
At t=0 the eigenphase is one and the initial state is recovered exactly.

cards.numerical_form: Diagonalize the Hermitian matrix once and evaluate eigenphases for all requested times.

cards.title: Site density and one-site entropy
cards.role: Produces the one-photon density and entropy panels.

checks.reason: The main text defines measured probabilities and one-site von Neumann entropy; Figs. S14-S17 show theory outputs.
In the one-particle sector rho_j=diag(1-p_j,p_j), so S_j=-p_j ln p_j-(1-p_j)ln(1-p_j).
Sum_j p_j=N follows from fixed-particle-number normalization.

cards.numerical_form: Compute occupations as probability-weighted basis values; use the binary entropy with 0*log(0)=0 for N=1.

cards.title: Connected z correlation and one-photon concurrence
cards.role: Produces the correlation and entanglement-spreading views of the one-photon wavefunction.

checks.reason: Main Eq. 2 defines concurrence and the supplement gives the reduced-density-matrix construction and connected correlation.
With sigma_z=2n-1 and no simultaneous occupation for i!=j, C^z_ij=-4p_i p_j; the two-site reduced state gives concurrence 2|c_i c_j|.
The formulas give |C^z_ij|<=1 and 0<=concurrence<=1 for normalized one-particle states.

cards.numerical_form: For i!=j compute -4*p_i*p_j and 2*abs(c_i*c_j); diagonal connected variance is 4*p_i*(1-p_i).

cards.title: Dispersion envelope and group velocity
cards.role: Connects the ballistic density front to the reported information-propagation speed.

checks.reason: Supplement Eqs. S28-S30 and Fig. S12 define the envelope fit and report 153.99 sites/us.
J in rad/ns gives sites/ns under the lattice-spacing-one convention; multiplying by 1000 gives sites/us.
The Table S1 open-chain spectrum gives 153.993429485 sites/us, matching the reported 153.99 within 2.23e-5 relative error.

cards.numerical_form: Diagonalize the 11-site Table S1 hopping matrix and evaluate the finite-difference derivative in Eq. S29 using delta_k=pi/(L+1).

cards.title: Two-particle correlator and double occupancy
cards.latex: G_{ij}=\langle a_i^\dagger a_j^\dagger a_i a_j\rangle;\quad G_{ii}=\langle n_i(n_i-1)\rangle
cards.role: Produces two-photon correlation matrices and verifies suppression of double occupancy.

checks.reason: Main Eq. 3 defines G_ij and Fig. S8 reports site-resolved double occupancy below 3%.
For i!=j the operator equals n_i n_j; for i=j bosonic commutation gives n_i(n_i-1).
For N=2, sum_ij G_ij=N(N-1)=2.

cards.numerical_form: Average n_i*n_j over basis probabilities off diagonal and n_i*(n_i-1) on diagonal; double-occupancy probability at i is P(n_i=2)=G_ii/2.

cards.title: Hard-core boson comparator
cards.role: Tests the paper's fermionization interpretation against an explicit occupancy-constrained limit.

checks.reason: The paper interprets |U/J| about 16-20 as hard-core behavior and compares it with free fermions.
Removing n_j=2 basis states is the finite-sector U-to-infinity limit and forces all diagonal double occupancy to zero.
The occupancy-capped Hamiltonian equals the full two-boson hopping Hamiltonian projected onto the no-double-occupancy subspace.

cards.numerical_form: Build the N=2 basis with max occupation one and the same hopping couplings; verify it equals the projected full-boson hopping Hamiltonian, then compare normalized off-diagonal G matrices with the calibrated-U run and U=0 run.

cards.title: Disordered on-site potentials and detuning-renormalized hopping

source_refs.value: Sec. IV.C, effect of unbalanced qubit frequencies

cards.role: Defines the 50-realization one- and two-photon disorder ensembles plotted in Figs. S9 and S10.

checks.reason: Supplement Sec. IV.C prints the uniform interval, the detuning-dependent hopping formula, six W values, and the 50-sequence average.
At W=0 every detuning vanishes and the effective hopping reduces exactly to the Table S1 coupling.
For detuning much larger than J, the effective hopping tends to zero, producing localization rather than faster spreading.

cards.numerical_form: For each printed W, independently sample 50 on-site vectors from the printed uniform interval, compute every effective bond from the printed formula, evolve the Table S1 Hamiltonian, and average site densities. A deterministic seed is selected independently as a reproducibility representative; source pixels are not used to select it.

cards.title: Coupling-error fidelity with optional Lindblad decoherence

source_refs.value: Sec. IV.E, measurement precision of nearest-neighbor coupling

cards.role: Produces the three ideal-versus-perturbed fidelity curves and the optional decoherence/disorder comparison in Fig. S11.

checks.reason: The supplement prints the fidelity definition, maximum plus/minus 2.5 percent coupling error, 0.5 MHz disorder width, and Table S1 T1/T2-star inputs.
For normalized nonnegative distributions, the Bhattacharyya coefficient F lies in [0,1].
With zero coupling error, zero disorder, and no collapse operators, p=q and F(t)=1 at every time.
The commutator and every Lindblad dissipator are trace preserving.

cards.numerical_form: Use one deterministic source-independent uniform coupling-error realization within plus/minus 2.5 percent for all three launches. For the dashed diagnostic, add an independently selected 0.5 MHz disorder realization and a standard Markovian T1/T2-star Lindblad model. The exact author seed and collapse-operator convention are not published, so this target remains reconstructed rather than author-realization exact.
open_questions: The publication does not give the coupling-error seed or distribution beyond the plus/minus 2.5 percent bound.
The publication names QuTiP and T1/T2-star but does not state the exact collapse-operator convention.
